title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is a typed English page numbered III.7, scanned upside down, from someone else's typescript, almost certainly a thesis or preprint on sheaves of separable or Azumaya algebras over a ringed space (X, A). Grothendieck evidently reused it as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages are his French manuscript notes on Hodge/Tannakian 'structures d'effectivité', cones in Γ' = Hom(G_m, G)/G, and the π_1 action.

The content, in modern language:
(1) For an A-algebra Γ with subalgebra Λ, the commutant (centralizer) is Γ^Λ = Hom_{Λ^e}(Λ, Γ).
(2) It quotes Auslander–Goldman ('The Brauer group of a commutative ring', 1960), Theorem 3.5, as reference [4]: if Γ is central separable (Azumaya) over A, and Λ ⊗_A Ω → Γ is an isomorphism, then Λ and Ω are each other's centralizers.
(3) It sheafifies the notion. For a sheaf of rings 𝒢 with center 𝒜 and an 𝒜-subalgebra ℒ, the commutant is the sheaf Hom_{ℒ^e}(ℒ, 𝒢), identified with a subsheaf of 𝒢 by evaluation at 1.
(4) Theorem III.7: for locally separable algebras ℒ, ℳ over (𝒜, α), ℒ is isomorphic to the commutant of ℳ in ℒ ⊗_𝒜 ℳ, and symmetrically.
(5) Start of the proof. It defines g: ℒ → Hom_{ℳ^e}(ℳ, ℒ ⊗ ℳ) by sending p ∈ ℒ(U) to the presheaf map q ↦ p|_V ⊗ q into the presheaf tensor product, then sheafifying. Next, finite presentation of ℳ is invoked, presumably to commute Hom with sheafification and stalks and so reduce to the local, ring-level Auslander–Goldman statement.

This is a routine sheaf-theoretic globalization of the Auslander–Goldman centralizer theorem. It belongs to the 1960s literature on Azumaya algebras over ringed spaces and the Brauer group of a sheaf/topos (Grothendieck, 'Le groupe de Brauer I', 1966; also student theses of that era).
errors: As stated, the theorem needs centrality. The centralizer of 1⊗ℳ in ℒ⊗_𝒜ℳ is (locally) ℒ⊗_𝒜 Z(ℳ), not ℒ, unless ℳ is central. So 'locally separable' must include 'central' in the author's definitions (i.e. Azumaya); otherwise the statement is false. This cannot be checked from this page alone.
The identification of Hom_{ℒ^e}(ℒ, 𝒢) with a subsheaf of 𝒢 (evaluation at 1) is correct but only asserted ('easily seen').
